youtube.title: Why Eyes Turn Red in Flash Photos 📸 #Shorts #science #facts #didyouknow
youtube.description:
Red-eye happens when a camera flash is close to the lens in a dim room. The pupils are wide open and cannot shrink in the instant before the flash. Light passes through the pupil and hits the back of the eye, where the retina sits on the choroid, a layer full of blood vessels. That blood reflects red light straight back into the camera.
